text:
incident-bot: Alert — spikes of CUDA illegal memory access observed on serving-runtime-prod-4 (node=gpu-18). 200+ errors/min, increased 5xx rate for the last 3m. Samples: /v1/generate.

oncall-ml: I'm on it. grabbing logs + core. @sara can you pause canary traffic?

sara: pausing canary now — reducing replicas to 0 for canary pool. :white_check_mark:  (kubectl scale deploy/serving-canary --replicas=0)

miguel: I'm checking node-level OOMs, `dmesg` shows: "GPU-0: illegal memory access at 0x7ff..." repeated. Also `nvidia-smi` shows process chew-up of memory then quick exit.

eng-runtime: log excerpt from container: ```
E 03:41:12 cuda_check: Illegal memory access (an illegal memory access was encountered)
Stack: serving_runtime::kv_cache::read+0x1f2
Backtrace: 0x7f8abc...
```

laura: any quick mitigation to reduce customer impact? fallback to CPU model or force a node reboot?

oncall-ml: CPU fallback looked promising in past. but that doubles latency. prod-impact numbers?

prod-support: ~3% of requests failing for tenants with long context (>=32k), impact concentrated in eu-west models. 2 paying customers seeing elevated error rates; rest have retries catching.

ops-bot: Automated cordon suggestion: `kubectl cordon gpu-18` recommended if node continues to produce illegal access.

miguel: repro attempt shows kernel panic not immediate; reproducible when sequence length > 64k and kv-cache hit pattern > 60%. suspect a race during pagewalk + kv cache eviction.

eng-runtime: can we flip to older runtime build? last successful build id: r-2025-11-08-9f3b. we can patch deployment to pin that image.

oncall-ml: I'm spinning up a CPU-only replica group and a pinned runtime in a new subset. Command: `kubectl set image deploy/serving-prod serving-runtime=redwood/serving:r-2025-11-08-9f3b --record`

sara: rolling pin started. routing rule updated to send 30% to pinned runtime, 70% to existing.

prod-support: drafting status page message: "We are investigating increased errors for long-context requests in EU; engineering is mitigating with fallbacks and node cordons. If you see persistent failures, contact support." share?

laura: +1 to sharing. include note about possible higher latency on CPU fallback.

eng-runtime: After pinning, error rate dropped to ~0.4% in 10m window. Node gpu-18 still intermittently produces illegal memory access on leftover pods. recommend cordon+drain and repro on isolated node.

miguel: executed `kubectl cordon gpu-18` and `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data gpu-18`. Repro no longer seen in prod traffic.

oncall-ml: collecting core dumps from drained pods. uploading to s3: s3://redwood-debug/4960001111/cores/. files: core.4572, core.4599.

eng-runtime: quick triage of the core: pointer in device-side pagewalk landed on misaligned pte table (GPU mmu). hypothesis: kernel nvmmu driver race introduced in recent kernel / cuda driver combo.

miguel: note: this only affects larger-context models using persistent KV cache path. smaller contexts unaffected.

prod-support: Customer impact update: two customers (AcmeCorp, LoomAI) experienced elevated error rates between 03:40–03:58 UTC, roughly 2.2k failed requests combined. We sent proactive notes to account teams.

laura: Ops recommendation: block upgrade path for the suspect runtime/kernel combo in EU until root cause confirmed. Also disable optimized KV-path for long-length requests as a software mitigation (feature-flag).

eng-runtime: opened bug #INC-2026-311 on infra board with core dump attached and repro steps. immediate actions: (1) keep gpu-18 cordoned (2) revert runtime on prod to pinned image (done) (3) add feature flag to disable persistent KV caching for contexts > 32k (in progress).

oncall-ml: set feature-flag in prod config: `SERVING_DISABLE_PERSISTENT_KV_FOR_LONG_CONTEXT=true` — staged, monitoring.

incident-bot: Incident annotated: labels: [cuda-illegal-memory, node-cordon, customer-impact]; severity: P2; runbook: serving-cuda-illegal.

sara: monitoring panels show tail errors down to baseline. will keep cordon for 6h and then attempt a controlled uncordon with extra log-collection.

prod-support: Status page update posted and customer messages sent. escalation to account execs done.

laura: follow-ups: schedule kernel/driver downgrade test matrix, validate pinned-runtime across zones, and add a synthetic long-context test to CI that runs nightly.

eng-runtime: assigning action items: miguel -> kernel repro + driver matrix, laura -> customer communications, sara -> cordon/un-cordon plan, oncall-ml -> roll out feature flag and monitor.

miguel: will also attempt to reproduce with instrumented driver to capture misaligned PTE before any rollback. will post logs here.

sara: thanks team. leaving cordon in place. marking thread resolved for active mitigation; will update if we uncordon or see regression. :white_check_mark:

prod-support: Closing note — no data exfiltration, only runtime failures. customers have been offered credits where SLAs were affected.

incident-bot: Archive scheduled in 72h unless reopened.
